scope: Read-only original issue/body/comments, ADR, persistent fixture contract and unchanged readers/controllers. No new test, producer, VM, Git or remote mutation.

decision.reason: The original persisted contract requires each original native/lifecycle run to pass unchanged validation before supplementary32-case behavior. Strict natural Job closure here explicitly includes native/supervisor/root exit0, not merely activeProcesses0. Current baseline x64 native1 and6steps6samples fails that contract. An x86 negative control would complete diagnostic coverage but could not convert these failed criteria into acceptance.
decision.minimumRecommendation: Keep #77 acceptance qualification open, report schema fix and candidate x64/x86 passes, preserve baseline failure and link the kernel liveness defect to #96 or its explicit follow-up. Do not execute a missing arm only to chase closure when the existing x64 control already makes all-four-pass unattainable.
decision.alternativeRequiresExplicitMaintainerSco: Maintainer may explicitly resolve #77 as schema-only with the unresolved baseline acceptance obligation superseded/transferred to a named kernel-maintenance issue. Such a close must say the prior acceptance criterion was not met and not claim four-arm pass. This is a scope change, not an inference that existing criteria allowed negative baseline.

originalText.issueBody:
The real MessagePort browser acceptance fixture fails before browser creation on both x64 and x86 with both baseline and candidate kernels: `Cannot register real browser observation action`.

The `acceptance.message-port.report` contract declares `caseId` and `status` as bounded-enum strings but omits the required `maxLength`. The existing SDK schema validator requires a maximum for every string, including strings with enums, and correctly rejects the fixture.

Add the missing limits based on the longest admitted enum values (24 for `worker-cooperative-close`, 11 for `unavailable`). Preserve the SDK validator, authorization, actual browser assertions, process cleanup predicates, and historical failed runs. Rebuild the real acceptance consumer for both architectures and rerun paired browser behavior checks before qualifying the fixture.

The durable fixture README, ADR and controllers define those preserved predicates precisely.
